visible.summary: Barbados demands real caution. Courts struck down the buggery laws in 2022; Barbados has an organised community (Equals, B-GLAD) and a functioning state. No LGR; modest social conservatism; tourist areas accustomed to diverse visitors.
visible.tangentialFactors: The 2022 court decriminalisation removed same-sex-conduct exposure for visitors travelling with partners.

sources.claim: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Human Dignity Trust page documents Eastern Caribbean constitutional challenges; Barbados decriminalised same-sex conduct in December 2022 via such a constitutional challenge.

Erasing 76 Crimes (Nov 2018): second Trans Day of Remembrance vigil held in Barbados (with NOW, local ally, veteran trans advocates named); trans activist Alexa Hoffmann's first-person account of visibility and danger on the island.

Erasing 76 Crimes (Apr 2019): sentencing in the violent meat-cleaver attack on trans activist Alexa Hoffmann — no jail time handed down; reported via Maurice Tomlinson and the Canadian HIV/AIDS Legal Network — an impunity outcome visitors should weigh.

Commentary (Aug 2020): trans Barbadians are frequently fired or denied jobs for 'dressing wrong'; the Employment (Protection from Discrimination) Bill does not cover them, and the island's 'Welcome Stamp' remote-work visa markets openness while anti-gay law stands.

Xtra (Jun 2018): Barbadian activists filed a constitutional challenge to the anti-gay laws with Hoffmann as claimant, supported by the Canadian HIV/AIDS Legal Network and the University of Toronto's international human-rights program.

visible.summary: Saint Kitts and Nevis demands real caution. Part of the Eastern Caribbean decriminalisation wave (2022 court ruling); tiny population, tourist economy, no documented anti-trans violence pattern; no LGR.
visible.tangentialFactors: The 2022 decriminalisation ruling removed same-sex-conduct exposure for visitors travelling with partners.
visible.outOfScopeNotes: Thin data; inherits Eastern Caribbean profile.

sources.claim: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Human Dignity Trust page documents Eastern Caribbean constitutional challenges; Saint Kitts and Nevis decriminalised same-sex conduct in 2022 via such a challenge.

Nation News (Aug 2022): the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court struck down anti-buggery laws - the ruling covering Saint Kitts and Nevis (Jamal Jeffers v Attorney General) decriminalised consensual same-sex conduct.

Outright country overview (updated 12 Mar 2026): consensual same-sex conduct legal throughout the country since 2022 — the High Court in Jamal Jeffers v The Attorney General struck Offences Against the Person Act s.56 (buggery) and s.57 (indecent assault against men) as contrary to privacy and expression rights; legal gender recognition is not possible; LGBTI organisations may register.

Saint Kitts and Nevis Alliance + ECADE UPR presentation (2025): decriminalisation in 2022 after civil-society court challenge; LGBTQ+ citizens included in the National Gender Equality Policy 2022-2027 but 'lack of tangible steps by the State'; discrimination in workplace, education, accommodation and hate speech still not illegal; LGBTQ+ people avoid law enforcement.

Country status page (fetched 2026-09-29): criminalisation of homosexuality rescinded in 2022; the penal code still contains no discrimination or harassment protections on sexual orientation or gender identity; same-sex unions are not recognised in any form (marriage or partnership), and same-sex households receive none of the rights afforded to opposite-sex married couples; gender identity recognition unavailable.

Tag archive (fetched 2026-09-29): Saint Kitts and Nevis collection led by 'Courts are the key to expanding LGBTQ rights in the Caribbean' and 'Lawsuits target 5 Caribbean nations' anti-gay laws' — advocacy coverage of the region's court-driven anti-sodomy-law challenges; the site tracks 66+ countries' anti-gay laws and reports no post-repeal discrimination statute for Saint Kitts and Nevis.

visible.summary: Dominica demands real caution. High Court decriminalised same-sex relations in April 2024 (fourth Eastern Caribbean state); the old law had allowed forced psychiatric commitment. No LGR; small community; no documented anti-trans violence pattern.
visible.tangentialFactors: The 2024 decriminalisation removed same-sex-conduct exposure for visitors travelling with partners.

sources.claim: Human Rights Watch dispatch (24 Apr 2024): Dominica's High Court of Justice in Roseau decriminalised same-sex conduct; the piece's headline call is for all Caribbean nations to repeal similar criminal laws.

BBC (23 Apr 2024): the High Court struck sections 14 and 16 of the Sexual Offences Act criminalising consensual same-sex activity as unconstitutional, on a case brought by a gay man living in Dominica; activists hailed 'a significant milestone in the ongoing struggle for LGBTQ rights in the Caribbean'.
NOTE: This is a State Department press statement page (archived, navigation only at fetch time); the underlying statement relates to Dominica.

US Mission Geneva (22 Mar 2011): statement on the Human Rights Council joint statement 'ending acts of violence and related human rights violations based on sexual orientation and gender identity', signed by 85 countries — the signatory list explicitly includes Dominica, a dated diplomatic commitment on the record.

Dominica News Online (20 Jul 2019): report of a High Court challenge to the buggery/sexual-activity laws filed by MiRiDom founder Daryl Phillip, announced at a news conference — contemporaneous evidence that the criminal provisions were under constitutional challenge five years before decriminalisation.

Erasing 76 Crimes (24 May 2013): Catholic Bishop Gabriel Malzaire of Dominica publicly called for eliminating criminal penalties for homosexuality and 'all forms of violence' against LGBT people, citing the Holy See's position — documented local religious-authority stance against criminalisation.

visible.summary: Saint Lucia demands real caution. The Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court struck down sodomy/gross-indecency laws in July 2025 (Randall Theodule v AG) — the region's most recent decriminalisation, welcomed by the IACHR. Saint Lucia has a relatively organised community (ECADE, United and Strong) and hosts Pride. No LGR.
visible.tangentialFactors: The July 2025 decriminalisation ruling removed same-sex-conduct exposure for visitors travelling with partners.

sources.claim: HRW (31 Jul 2025): the Saint Lucia High Court decriminalized same-sex conduct — struck down the criminal provision as unconstitutional (Eastern Caribbean strategic litigation); visitor-facing criminal exposure for consensual same-sex conduct ended.

NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Human Dignity Trust case digest covers Randall Theodule et al. v. the Attorney General of Saint Lucia - the constitutional challenge that decriminalised same-sex conduct.

Erasing 76 Crimes (4 Apr 2017): Caribbean LGBTI activists — United and Strong of St Lucia and ECADE — protested a PinkNews item (28 Mar 2017) framing regional sexuality, under the banner 'Nothing about us without us'; documents regional civil-society pushback against outsider framing of Caribbean LGBT issues.
AP News: St Lucia court ruling that criminalising gay sex is unconstitutional - the Eastern Caribbean litigation striking down the colonial-era law (page largely navigation content at fetch time).

United and Strong St Lucia (21 May 2015): human-rights sensitisation training for law enforcement held Castries 19 May 2015 — officers from RSLPF, Air and Sea Ports, Customs and Bordelais Correctional facility, with CariFLAGS, the Canadian HIV-AIDS Legal Network and Maurice Tomlinson; builds on 2014 sensitisation work.

visible.summary: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines demands real caution — the Eastern Caribbean outlier: its High Court UPHELD the buggery laws in 2024 (unlike its neighbours), so criminalisation (10 years) remains formally in force. Enforcement is rare, but the legal floor and judicial hostility distinguish it from the decriminalised neighbours.
visible.tangentialFactors: The buggery laws (10 years, upheld 2024) remain a formal exposure for visitors travelling with partners.
visible.outOfScopeNotes: 2024 ruling upheld criminalisation — opposite trajectory from neighbours.

sources.claim: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Human Dignity Trust page documents Eastern Caribbean constitutional challenges; Saint Vincent and the Grenadines retains colonial-era buggery and gross-indecency laws.

GlobalGayz country profile: consensual homosexual acts between adults in private remain criminal under the British-inherited Buggery Act; many gay men marry women and live 'down-low'; social infrastructure is thin, with HIV-prevention groups (Caribbean HIV/AIDS Alliance) the main contact point for MSM -- undated snapshot of social climate and legal shadow.

PinkNews (17 Feb 2024): the High Court ruled on 16 Feb 2024 to uphold the ban on gay sex (sections 146/148 of the criminal code), dismissing a constitutional challenge -- same-sex conduct stays criminal in St Vincent and the Grenadines.

HRW (20 Jul 2023), 58-page report 'They Can Harass Us Because of the Laws': LGBT people in SVG face bias-motivated violence and discrimination in daily life; HRW calls for decriminalising gay sex and passing SOGI non-discrimination legislation -- core rights documentation for the country.

ECADE press release (19 Feb 2024): the Eastern Caribbean rights alliance condemns the 16 Feb 2024 High Court ruling upholding the same-sex conduct ban, saying LGBTQ+ Vincentians face greater vulnerability -- regional civil-society reaction with dated ruling outcome.

visible.summary: Grenada demands real caution. The buggery law (10 years) remains on the books (no successful court challenge yet), though unenforced; no LGR; small community; tourist areas insulated.
visible.tangentialFactors: The buggery law (10 years, unenforced) remains a formal exposure for visitors travelling with partners.

sources.claim: The Advocates for Human Rights + Khaleem Ali + GrenCHAP UPR stakeholder report (Oct 2024) on LGBTIQ+ rights in Grenada: documents the legal and social situation for the UN review, including Sections 430/431 criminal provisions, and GrenCHAP's 15+ years of service to marginalised groups (LGBT+, PLHIV, sex workers, vulnerable youth).

Outright International profile (updated Mar 2026): same-sex conduct criminalised under Sections 430 ('grossly indecent act') and 431 ('unnatural crime'); no legal gender recognition; no anti-discrimination protections; LGBTIQ people face discrimination in housing, education, employment and public services, and fear of prosecution inhibits reporting to police.

US State Dept 2023 report on Grenada: significant human-rights issues include laws criminalising consensual sexual conduct between men, though not enforced; no arbitrary killings, torture or disappearances reported.
